core.text: Deponents give orders with **the deponent command forms (sequere! = follow!, sequimini! = follow, all of you!)**. To one person the command ends in -re: *sequere!* (follow!), *laetāre!* (rejoice!), *intuēre!* (look!). To several it ends in -minī: *sequiminī!*, *laetāminī!*, *intuēminī!* — the same as the passive 'you all' ending. Latin name: *imperativus verborum deponentium*.
A command in English is the bare verb: *follow me!* Latin needs the right ending for one listener or many.
Singular: present stem + -re (laetāre, intuēre, sequere, partīre). Plural: present stem + -minī (laetāminī, intuēminī, sequiminī, partīminī).

*Sequere* looks like an active **the infinitive (the 'to' form)** of a third-conjugation verb (*legere*), but *sequī* is deponent and its infinitive is *sequī*; so *sequere* can only be a command. Rule of thumb: if the dictionary form ends in -ī, a form in -re is 'do it!', not 'to do'.

more.text: The learner's notes (week 25 review) put it as: the deponent infinitive-lookalike is the singular command (*intuērī → intuēre*, *cōnsōlārī → cōnsōlāre*, *cōnfitērī → cōnfitēre*), the plural uses -minī (*intuēminī, sequiminī, laetēminī*).

Ørberg (cap. XXV) lines them up against active commands: *laetāre! = gaudē!*, *intuēre! = spectā!*, *revertere! = redī!*, *partīre! = dīvide!*. For 'don't', use *nōlī / nōlīte* + deponent infinitive: *nōlī mīrārī!*
